messages.author: 4c8abebaa7e886e1
messages.subject: strange behaviour in simple model
parts:
As an example for how to write R-inla commands I generated the following data

set.seed(1)
m<-100*20
x<-rnorm(m)
area<-sample(seq(1,20),size=m,replace=T)
#parameter values
#random effect precision
tau.v0 <- 2
tau.v1 <- 1.5
#fixed effect
b0 <- 5
b1 <- 2
#overall precision
tau <- 3

v0 <- rnorm(length(unique(area)),mean=0,sd=(1/sqrt(tau.v0)))
v1 <- rnorm(length(unique(area)),mean=0,sd=(1/sqrt(tau.v1)))
#allocate the area effect to each observation
v1j<- v1[area]
v0j<- v0[area]

#y with a random intercept + slope model
#generate y with mean the model and some variance
y <- rnorm(m, mean=(b0+v0j)+(b1+v1j)*x, sd=(1/sqrt(tau)))

#make a data frame to pass to inla
ris.data<-data.frame(y=y, x=x, area=area)

I then put a very basic model with a random intercept and fixed slope

ri.formula <- y ~ 1 + x + f(area, model="iid")

ri.inla<-inla(ri.formula,
              family="gaussian",
              data=ris.data)

Then I look at the results:

round(ri.inla$summary.fixed[,c(1:3,5)],3)

sometimes (even with the same value for set.seed) I get sensible results but most of the time I get really high values for the sd of the fixed effects. What is going on? I feel I am missing something fundamental. 

Running R 4.2.2. 

Thanks,
Sara

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] strange behaviour in simple model
parts:
I think the model is not well defined as you have two terms fighting
against each other, the 'area' and the 'gaussian noise', and you need to
tell what you want/believe in the priors for these two precisions. f.ex
that 'area' should be contracted to variance=0, like here


ri.formula <- y ~ 1 + x + f(area, model="iid",
hyper = list(prec = list(
prior = "pc.prec",
param = c(1, 0.01))))

messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] strange behaviour in simple model
parts:
Here's a few changes to fit the model in manner consistent with the simulation:

ris.data<-data.frame(y=y, x=x, x2=x,area=area)
ri.formula <- y ~ 1 + f(area) + x + f(x2,area)

All looks fine now.

John
